extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys and agents registered to practice before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (PTO); PTO enrollment & discipline staff; administrative law practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural rules governing discipline of patent practitioners before the USPTO, including what conduct constitutes violations (neglect, dishonesty, inadequate preparation, failure to notify, mishandling client property, habitual violations), service/complaint procedures, and factors for choosing penalties (suspension/exclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of address to OED (37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any registered attorney or agent must notify the OED Director of his or her postal address for the office and every change to any of said addresses within thirty days of the date of the change by separately filing written notice of the change to the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners who fail to provide an up-to-date address risk defective service of disciplinary complaints; service is measured against the address provided to OED.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper service of complaint (37 C.F.R. § 11.35(a)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper service in a disciplinary proceeding is 'any delivery service that provides ability to confirm delivery or attempted delivery' to a respondent at the address provided to OED.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: certified mail with return receipt is acceptable; certificate of service should show compliance. Proof of receipt (e.g., signed domestic return receipt) supports that service was completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint content requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint must inform the respondent of the allegations against him, the opportunity to file an answer within thirty days from the date of the complaint, and that failure to answer may result in admission of the allegations and a default judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaint must name respondent, give a plain and concise description of allegations, state the appropriate address for delivery, the addressee, and limited time for filing an answer. The complaint should include the explicit warning that default judgment may be entered if no timely answer is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default judgment/admission for failure to answer (37 C.F.R. § 11.36(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent's failure to answer a complaint constitutes an admission of each allegation in the complaint, and default judgment may be entered against the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When default is entered, allegations in the complaint and supporting motion/exhibits are incorporated into the order; failure to answer waives rights to further administrative and judicial review if appeal not timely filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect of legal matter (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not neglect a legal matter entrusted to the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative misconduct: allowing patent applications to become abandoned without client consent; failing to timely respond to PTO correspondence (Office Actions, Notices of Abandonment); failing to communicate with clients about significant status changes; failing to take corrective steps to revive abandoned applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling a matter without adequate preparation (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not handle a legal matter without preparation adequate in the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of inadequate preparation: failing to produce sufficient evidence to substantiate claimed mailings to the PTO; failing to supply adequate evidence in support of a petition for revival; filing informal status enquiries instead of required formal petitions to revive applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific examples: falsely representing to the PTO or clients that responses, amendments, or payments were mailed/received; falsely claiming not to have received Notices of Allowance or other PTO communications. Such false statements to the PTO or clients support discipline under this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) and 10.23(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not engage in any other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office; conduct includes failing to inform a client of correspondence received from the Office when (i) it could have a significant effect on a matter pending before the Office, (ii) it is received by the practitioner on behalf of the client, and (iii) a reasonable practitioner would believe the client should be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifying clients of Notices of Abandonment and other time-sensitive communications is obligatory. Failure to do so constitutes conduct that reflects adversely on fitness to practice and may be disciplined under 10.23(b)(6) and 10.23(c)(8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitual or intentional violation of disciplinary rules (provisions cited e.g., 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.77(b), 10.77(c), 10.23(b)(4), 10.23(b)(6), 10.89(c)(6)/10.59(c)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not intentionally or habitually violate any provision of the subchapter or established rules of evidence; repeated or continuous violations over time support enhanced discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of multiple, repeated infractions over a multi-year period is an aggravating factor that can justify substantial sanctions (including exclusion). The decision cites the practitioner's six-year pattern of repeated violations as supporting exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt delivery of client property (37 C.F.R. § 10.112(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall promptly pay or deliver to the client as requested the funds, securities, or other property in the possession of the practitioner which the client is entitled to receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retaining client files or property after termination of representation is prohibited absent a bona fide entitlement or dispute; failing to return valuable client application materials after requests is a violation and an aggravating factor for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and authority to discipline (35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D); 35 U.S.C. § 32; 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.32, 11.34, 11.39)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTO may establish regulations governing recognition and conduct of agents/attorneys before the Office; any person not complying with regulations may be suspended or excluded after notice and opportunity for a hearing; disciplinary actions are initiated by filing a complaint with a hearing officer in accordance with the cited regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the statutory/regulatory basis for proceedings and penalties (suspension/exclusion) and indicates the procedural framework for bringing disciplinary actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty determination factors (37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b)(1)-(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining an appropriate penalty the presiding officer must consider: (1) whether the practitioner violated a duty owed to a client/public/legal system/profession; (2) whether the practitioner acted intentionally, knowingly, or negligently; (3) the amount of actual or potential injury caused; and (4) the existence of aggravating or mitigating factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes considering foreseeability of potential injury (ABA Standards for Imposing Lawyer Sanctions) and weighing number/severity of violations, actual vs. speculative harm, and any history of prior discipline or aggravating conduct when choosing between suspension and exclusion. Exclusion is justified where repeated, deliberate violations cause or risk substantial harm and lesser sanctions would not protect the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities and procedures on suspension/exclusion and reinstatement (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58, 11.60; appellate timing per § 11.55)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners are directed to the rules concerning responsibilities in case of suspension or exclusion (11.58), petitions for reinstatement (11.60), and the requirement to file an appeal with the PTO Director within thirty days including exceptions to the ALJ's decision (11.55).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After exclusion, a practitioner must follow the specified administrative responsibilities and may petition for reinstatement per the regulations; failure to timely appeal is deemed acceptance of the initial decision and waiver of further review.
